subject: APAC-EU jurisdictional switchover criteria and cold-region activation
messages:
From: ops+platform@acme.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: j.lee@globex.com
Date: 2028-06-30T03:12:00Z
Subject: Request: criteria for triggering APAC->EU cold-region activation

Sergio,

Quick one from our platform team: we need a clear, documented set of criteria that will cause Acme's private deployment in APAC to be routed to the EU cold region (jurisdictional switchover). Procurement and legal want explicit thresholds and evidence we can show auditors.

Specifically we need:
- The precise operational triggers (network partition, control plane unreachable, KMS failover conditions)
- The expected impact on latency and availability (SLO delta)
- A short checklist of evidence items (audit logs, route change artifacts)
- Any required customer-facing timelines (how long before we cut over)

Can your team validate the criteria and share a one-page summary + runbook stub by EOD Friday? We referenced your public residency doc but need account-specific guardrails.

Thanks,
Chris Patel
Platform Engineering | Acme Financial

Attachment: none
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: ops+platform@acme.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-30T07:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: criteria for triggering APAC->EU cold-region activation

Chris — thanks for the ask. Looping in Marissa (networking) and Vivek (private deployments/SLA) to validate.

High level plan: we will propose a 3-tier trigger matrix (Immediate, Graceful, Manual) with concrete signals per tier. Initial items below — we'll produce the one-page summary + runbook stub by EOD Fri as requested.

Immediate (auto-trigger, <30s reaction):
- Control-plane TLS/API endpoint returns 5xx for > 30s across 3 AZs in APAC region
- KV cache invalidation/failure that causes >50% request errors on a healthy node pool

Graceful (automated with cooldown, minutes):
- Sustained latency increase >= 3x P50 and token failure rate >5% for 5 minutes
- Inter-region WAN packet loss > 25% for 2 consecutive minutes with route flaps

Manual (operator-driven):
- Legal/Incident commander authorizes due to regulatory directive or active investigation

I'll attach the draft runbook and a minimal network diagram for evidence items. Marissa — can you confirm the network signals and add the BGP/peering checklist? Vivek — can you call out any SLA exceptions that require signoff?

— Sergio
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Attachments: activation_runbook_v1.pdf (draft), network-diagram-APAC-EU.png
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, ops+platform@acme.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-30T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: criteria for triggering APAC->EU cold-region activation

Adding technical detail to Sergio's matrix — revised signals and evidence items from networking/op side: 

Network signals we recommend as canonical evidence (order of preference):
1) BGP session DOWN to >=2 eBGP peers + BFD detect (session flaps and no DMARC from transit)
2) Proven route leak or blackhole (RPKI/ROA mismatch logs + flow logs showing 0x0 acceptance)
3) Inter-region packet loss >25% and RTT increase >150ms sustained for 3 minutes

Operational artifacts to capture and archive (for auditors):
- Route-change diff (pre/post) exported from edge routers (attach as text file)
- VPC flow logs showing egress to EU endpoint and timestamps
- Frontend and agent traces showing attempted reconnection and error codes
- Control plane audit events: token issuance failures, control API 5xx logs

KMS and data custody notes:
- KMS key replication is asynchronous; a KMS failover alone is NOT an auto-trigger unless key unwrap failures exceed 10% across authenticated requests for >5m.
- If customer-managed keys are in play, legal sign-off required before any automatic key rewrapping or export.

I've attached the network diagram and a KMS checklist (spreadsheet) — these contain the exact log paths and retention windows we recommend storing for 180 days.

Marissa Cole
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-replication-checklist.xlsx, network-diagram-APAC-EU.png
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: ops+platform@acme.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-30T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: criteria for triggering APAC->EU cold-region activation

Couple of enterprise constraints to call out (SLA / contractual):
- Automatic Immediate triggers will cause a temporary SLO penalty for the customer (we estimate p95 token latency increases by ~220ms and token cost by ~8%). We can't enable auto-trigger for paid Dedicated customers without a signed SLA amendment.
- For Private (VPC) customers on annual contracts, we require a 48-hour notification window to change routing behavior unless the trigger meets the Immediate criteria above.

Escalation/approval flow we propose:
1) If Immediate conditions fire, the system will create an Incident and auto-notify the customer's on-call + Redwood ops. Legal and account execs get an FYI.
2) For Graceful triggers, an automated mitigation (cache-bypass) runs and a ticket is created; a human operator must confirm before outbound routing changes to the cold region.

Naomi — please prepare a one-page compliance evidence checklist we can hand to Acme's auditors (include log retention windows, fields to export, and recommended SigV formats). We'll include that with the runbook submission.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick, clear responses — this is exactly what Acme needs. Two quick clarifications before EOD Fri deliverable:
1) For Immediate auto-trigger: will Redwood surface a signed auditable token (hash + timestamp) that shows the exact control-plane 5xx condition that instigated the switch? We need that for our SOC artifacts.
2) For KMS-managed keys: can you confirm if replication lag metrics are published to the same control plane dashboard or whether we should pull them separately from the KMS provider?

If you can answer those two items inline, we'll mark this as priority and sync legal for the SLA amendment language.

Chris
Chris Patel | Platform Engineering, Acme Financial
